_README: You write the anchors. Each one asserts a causal claim -- this old state,
plus this event, gives this new state -- and that claim is YOURS, not an
LLM's. The generator only puts it into words.
REQUIREMENTS PER ATTRIBUTE
states: at least THREE, so counterfactual and conflict conditions can be
built. Each needs a single-token `label` (verified against the
tokenizer at build time) -- `transit`, not `public_transit`.
Multi-token labels make logit-lens trajectories at the decision
token unreadable.
events: at least TWO from the same old state, leading to DIFFERENT new
states. Without this you cannot tell computing f(S,E) apart from
memorising E -> new_state.
EVENT WRITING RULES
- never name any state label, in any form
- describe what happened, never what the person now wants
- one causal step: a reader should not need two inferences
- `type` is from the taxonomy below; used for per-type analysis
TAXONOMY
constraint   the old option becomes harmful or impossible
resource     what the old option required is gone
environment   surroundings changed
goal          a new goal conflicts with the old option
experience    a bad experience with the old option

events.effect: car ownership becomes unaffordable
events.note: insurance, repairs and parking now consume most of the monthly budget

events.effect: daily destinations become close enough to reach without a car
events.note: a move puts work, shops and appointments within a few kilometres

events.effect: using a bike becomes medically unsafe
events.note: a wrist fracture leaves the person unable to support weight on handlebars

events.effect: the route becomes unsafe for bicycles
events.note: major construction removes the only protected route and diverts traffic onto narrow roads

events.effect: a new job requires frequent trips between sites beyond the rail network
events.note: the role involves carrying equipment to several locations each day

events.effect: repeated impact becomes harmful
events.note: a torn meniscus leads the physiotherapist to prohibit high-impact training

events.effect: outdoor exertion becomes unsafe during much of the year
events.note: a move brings months of extreme heat while an indoor aquatic facility is nearby

events.effect: a new competitive target requires sustained land-based mileage
events.note: the person registers for an event whose preparation depends on progressively longer distances on foot

events.effect: repeated arm strokes become painful
events.note: a rotator cuff injury makes overhead movement medically restricted

events.effect: the required facility is no longer available
events.note: the local aquatic centre closes indefinitely while a safe cycle network remains accessible

events.effect: the time available to read messages collapses
events.note: the person now reads between dispatch calls with only seconds available

events.effect: messages must be scanned and passed to another person
events.note: replies are copied into shift handovers where colleagues need the main points immediately

events.effect: decisions must now be documented and defensible
events.note: a new regulated role requires reasoning and assumptions to be recorded

events.effect: messages are now consumed on a very small screen during short interruptions
events.note: the person loses desktop access and checks replies mainly while travelling

events.effect: the information must be reused as a teaching aid
events.note: responses are now shared with trainees who need key steps separated clearly

events.effect: music is now used primarily to sustain concentration during demanding work
events.note: the person begins spending long sessions writing and finds prominent vocals distracting

events.effect: a new live experience reveals a strong attraction to improvisation
events.note: after attending several small ensemble performances, the person becomes absorbed by spontaneous solos

events.effect: high-intensity sound worsens an existing sleep problem
events.note: a clinician recommends avoiding stimulating audio in the evening

events.effect: the main listening context changes to quiet late-night study
events.note: complex rhythmic changes repeatedly interrupt concentration while working

events.effect: a new performance experience makes highly interactive playing especially compelling
events.note: a friend takes the person to a series of small sessions where musicians respond spontaneously to one another

events.effect: a new project requires understanding technical concepts
events.note: the person begins work on a project involving genetics and needs background knowledge

events.effect: a family project requires understanding a past period
events.note: while tracing relatives, the person needs to learn about the places and decades in which they lived

events.effect: a series of heavily disputed accounts undermines trust in the material
events.note: the person repeatedly discovers that books they enjoyed contained major factual errors

events.effect: the surrounding community now discusses technical discoveries and provides accessible material
events.note: a move into a research-oriented workplace brings frequent recommendations and a well-stocked technical library

events.effect: mentally demanding material becomes difficult to tolerate after a major increase in cognitive workload
events.note: the person spends the day analysing dense technical documents and has little concentration left afterward

states.label: cities
states.gloss: urban destinations with museums and restaurants

states.label: resorts
states.gloss: destinations centred on rest and amenities

events.effect: a period of severe work exhaustion makes highly scheduled trips unmanageable
events.note: after months of overtime, the person needs a trip with minimal planning and few decisions

events.effect: a new hobby requires access to landscapes and wildlife
events.note: the person begins a serious photography project focused on animals and natural scenery

events.effect: a series of overcrowded trips makes dense tourist areas aversive
events.note: long queues and packed streets repeatedly dominate recent holidays

events.effect: long walks over uneven ground become temporarily unsafe
events.note: an ankle injury requires several months without strenuous hiking

events.effect: a new academic interest requires visiting museums and historic buildings
events.note: the person starts studying architecture and wants to see major works in person

states.label: batching
states.gloss: preparing many meals at once for later

events.effect: weekday meal preparation time disappears but one long weekly session remains available
events.note: a new commute leaves evenings crowded while Sunday afternoons remain free

events.effect: the kitchen becomes unusable
events.note: a plumbing failure leaves the home without a working stove or sink for several weeks

events.effect: a new financial target requires sharply reducing discretionary spending
events.note: the person begins saving for a major purchase and reviews how much prepared meals cost each month

events.effect: the person must regularly provide food for a large group with limited time
events.note: a weekly community activity now requires bringing enough food for many participants

events.effect: a dangerous accident creates a strong aversion to using the kitchen
events.note: a serious oil fire during meal preparation causes significant damage and anxiety

events.effect: the new work requires resolving urgent issues immediately
events.note: delays of even an hour can halt operations and decisions often require rapid back-and-forth

events.effect: the person is frequently away from a computer and has only brief opportunities to respond
events.note: a new routine involves moving between sites throughout the day

events.effect: understanding speech over a connection becomes unreliable
events.note: a hearing change makes compressed telephone audio difficult to distinguish

events.effect: important decisions now require a permanent searchable record
events.note: a compliance process requires agreements and approvals to be documented

events.effect: repeated misunderstandings in short written exchanges cause serious conflict
events.note: several important relationships are damaged after tone is repeatedly misread in messages

events.effect: the new skill is evaluated through physical performance rather than recall
events.note: a certification requires completing a series of procedures under observation

events.effect: written instructions repeatedly fail to clarify spatial movements
events.note: the person struggles to understand how tools should be positioned from text alone

events.effect: reliable high-speed internet becomes unavailable
events.note: a move leaves the household with a slow connection that cannot reliably stream lessons

events.effect: the equipment required for hands-on work is no longer accessible
events.note: the workshop closes and replacement equipment is too expensive to obtain

events.effect: the available preparation window becomes too short for repeated attempts
events.note: an unexpected deadline leaves only a few evenings to cover a large amount of material

states.label: markets
states.gloss: buying from local markets and vendors

events.effect: nearby retail access disappears
events.note: a move places the nearest major shops several hours away

events.effect: a new cooking project requires unusually fresh seasonal ingredients
events.note: the person begins preparing meals whose ingredients change with the local harvest

events.effect: repeated delivery failures make remote purchases unreliable
events.note: several expensive orders arrive damaged, late, or not at all

events.effect: walking through large outdoor shopping areas becomes temporarily difficult
events.note: a leg injury prevents prolonged walking and carrying bags

events.effect: regular interactions with local vendors create a strong positive experience
events.note: after attending a neighbourhood event, the person develops relationships with several producers
